extracted.intended_audience: public company registrants, corporate counsel, disclosure preparers, auditors, and compliance officers preparing SEC filings
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and rules for registrants to calculate, disclose, and file greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions metrics (Scopes 1 and 2, intensity metrics, methodology, boundaries, and timing) in SEC filings under the final climate disclosure rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emissions intensity metrics
rubrics_metrics.description: Emissions intensity metrics are required to be in terms of metric tons of CO2e per unit of total revenue and per unit of production for the fiscal year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule contemplates two intensity metrics (per unit of revenue and per unit of production) expressed as metric tons CO2e per the relevant unit for the fiscal year. (Original phrasing: “to be in terms of metric tons of CO2e per unit of total revenue and per unit of production for the fiscal year.”)

rubrics_metrics.name: Permitted standards and flexibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants have flexibility to leverage standards of their choice in calculating and disclosing GHG emissions metrics required by the final rules, including the GHG Protocol or relevant ISO standards, or other standards that may be established over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release explicitly recognizes the GHG Protocol and ISO 14064 (and related ISO standards) and states the final rules' definitions are intended to include substantially similar emissions as those measured pursuant to the ISO standards. Registrants may therefore rely on well-established standards or future standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 1 and Scope 2 definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: For the purposes of the final rules, “Scope 1 emissions” and “Scope 2 emissions” are defined, respectively, as a registrant's direct emissions and indirect emissions largely from the generation of purchased or acquired electricity consumed by the registrant's operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The definitions are intended to include substantially similar emissions as those measured pursuant to ISO standards. See also cross-reference to 17 CFR 229.1500 for formal definitions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Materiality-based disclosure of Scope 1 and Scope 2
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant's Scope 1 emissions are material but its Scope 2 emissions are not material, the registrant must disclose Scope 1 and is not required to disclose Scope 2 (and vice versa). If both are material, it must disclose both categories of emissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Materiality drives the obligation to disclose each Scope; registrants must assess materiality separately for Scope 1 and Scope 2.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exemptions for EGCs and SRCs
rubrics_metrics.description: Emerging growth companies (EGCs) and smaller reporting companies (SRCs) will not be required to disclose their Scopes 1 and 2 emissions under the final rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final rule explicitly exempts EGCs and SRCs from the Scope 1 and 2 disclosure requirement (see 17 CFR 229.1505(a)(3)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Organizational boundaries requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Organizational boundaries are defined in the final rule to mean the boundaries that determine the operations owned or controlled by a registrant for the purpose of calculating its GHG emissions and are required to be consistent with the scope of entities included in its consolidated financial statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule’s organizational-boundaries approach may differ from the GHG Protocol, which permits choice between equity share, operational control, or financial control methods. Commenters noted this difference could increase compliance burden; the rule requires consistency with consolidated financial-statement boundaries (see 17 CFR 229.1505(b)(1)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Operational boundaries requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Operational boundaries are defined to mean the boundaries that determine the direct and indirect emissions associated with the business operations owned or controlled by a registrant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Operational boundaries determine which direct and indirect sources are included in Scope calculations. See 17 CFR 229.1500 for the formal definition and 17 CFR 229.1505(b)(1)(ii) for application.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emission factors and activity data
rubrics_metrics.description: Emission factors are ratios that typically relate GHG emissions to a proxy measure of activity at an emissions source (e.g., kWh of electricity, quantity of fuel, output, hours of operation, distance travelled, floor area).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The EPA has published commonly used emission factors (EPA, Emission Factors for Greenhouse Gas Inventories, Apr. 2021). The rule references 17 CFR 229.1500 for the definition of “emission factors” and encourages use of established emission-factor sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope 2 calculation methods (market-based vs location-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Two common methods for calculating Scope 2 emissions for purchased electricity are the market-based method and the location-based method.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrant should select and disclose the methodology used; sources cited include the GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance (Chapter 7) and EPA Center for Corporate Climate Leadership guidance. The choice affects inclusion of instruments such as RECs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment of RECs and offsets in gross emissions
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule specifies that gross emissions should be calculated without taking into account any purchased or generated offsets; the extent to which a registrant will exclude RECs from its gross emissions will depend on the methodology the registrant chooses to use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants are required to describe their methodology and, for Scope 2, include a description of whether and how RECs factor into its gross emissions calculation. (See also the GHG Protocol Scope 2 Guidance and related EPA materials.)

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to describe methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant is required to describe its methodology used to calculate GHG emissions metrics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disclosure should include methodology choices (e.g., organizational and operational boundaries, Scope 2 method chosen, treatment of RECs/offsets), assumptions, use of emission factors, and any estimation approaches. The rule points to established guidance documents for methodology descriptions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowance for estimates and flexibility in methodology
rubrics_metrics.description: The use of estimates is supported because measurement of emissions usually includes many estimates, assumptions, and extrapolations of data; some commenters and professional services firms supported maximum flexibility in reporting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The release notes support from commenters (e.g., PWC, KPMG, BIO) for allowing estimates and methodological flexibility given the evolving ecosystem of GHG reporting; registrants should document assumptions and estimation methods.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accommodations for information unknown or not reasonably available
rubrics_metrics.description: To the extent Scope 1 and/or 2 emissions disclosure are required, accommodations for information that is unknown and not reasonably available may be available under 17 CFR 230.409 or 17 CFR 240.12b-21, if their conditions are met.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants may rely on statutory/regulatory accommodations for unavailable information subject to the conditions of the cited CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing, transition periods, and filing deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing rules include transition periods (e.g., large accelerated filers (LAFs) have a one-year transition period before being required to comply with the GHG emissions disclosure requirements; other accelerated filers (AFs) not SRCs or EGCs comply two years after LAFs) and specific filing deadlines for incorporating disclosures into SEC forms.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples and mechanics: registrants must include GHG emissions metrics disclosure in Form 10-K by the applicable deadline; a registrant may include disclosures in an amended Form 10-K filed no later than the due date for its second quarter Form 10-Q. For registration statements (e.g., Form S-3/F-3) the GHG emissions disclosure must be as of the most recently completed fiscal year that is at least 225 days prior to the effectiveness date; the release provides example calendar-date math and illustrative scenarios.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment when a registrant becomes an LAF during the fiscal year
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant becomes an LAF during the fiscal year, it must present the disclosures for the most recently completed fiscal year in which it became an LAF; it is not required to provide those disclosures for prior fiscal years included in its filing when it was not an LAF to the extent that information was not previously required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This rule recognizes changes in filer status mid-year and limits retroactive reporting obligations to the fiscal year in which the new status applies.
